about: Private counts per UTC day, default 30 days, up to 365, newest first; totals adds up the days listed (without callers, which can't be added across days). hours: calls in each UTC hour, 00 to 23 (null: not recorded); in totals, each hour added up across the days. failed_hours (from 0.10.1): the calls whose outcome was failed, in each UTC hour; refused_hours (from 0.10.1): the requests counted in per_ip_refusals, in each UTC hour; both null on days before 0.10.1 and, on the day it started, for the hours before that; not in totals. Each tool's calls = ok (found something; for alternatives, verified replacements) + similar_only (only similar parts for manual comparison, no verified replacements) + not_found (worked, found nothing) + bad_request (the request was invalid) + rate_limited (a limit turned it away) + failed (something broke on this server or a service it calls), plus unsorted where shown (error replies from before 0.6.4, which weren't sorted). callers counts distinct IPs, which isn't the number of people: hosted apps such as claude.ai call from their own servers' IPs, and a caller seen before and after a restart counts twice. apps are the names MCP apps send when they connect. The stats keep no IPs, whole queries or individual lookup numbers; popular_terms can include part-number tokens once they reach its caller threshold. Cutover 2026-10-26: alternatives replies before that date counted similar-parts-only replies as not found; historical counts have not been reclassified. reasons (from 0.9.0; earlier days have none): for each tool, why calls came back not_found or failed, one fixed label a call. why_empty: how the checks behind jlc_search's why_empty went (no_counterfactual: no library, package or stock limit to test). distributors retry_found and retry_missed: before 0.9.3, DigiKey all-digit numbers that missed the direct lookup and went on to a keyword search, also counted in sent. distributors skipped (from 0.10.0, on days with any): part numbers not sent because no distributor can list them (a value such as 10k, a BOM placeholder, an LCSC code, non-ASCII text, not 3-40 characters); one a number. From 0.10.0 (earlier days have none): upstream, for each service this server calls: jlcpcb (parts search), lcsc (product data), easyeda_products (footprint checks), easyeda_components (symbols and footprints for pinouts), easyeda_pads (footprint pads for land checks), cse (SamacSys searches and model downloads) and, from 0.10.4, digikey (DigiKey's HTTP requests; distributors counts lookups); sent is HTTP requests sent, one each, not tool calls; retries the further attempts the HTTP client made on its own for them, where it reports them (a timeout reports none); cached answers given without a request (memory cache, on-disk store or seed); rate_limited requests this server's own budget or pause for that service kept back (for cse, also sent model downloads SamacSys refused for quota); waited (from 0.10.4) requests sent after waiting for a free request slot. parts_asked: part numbers asked for with Mouser and DigiKey, whether stored answers gave them, a request did or the limits turned them away (total; skipped ones aren't counted), and how many were different that day (distinct, ignoring case and - _ /; counted through salted hashes held in memory, so a restart counts them again; not in totals, which can't add them across days). per_ip_refusals: HTTP requests admission control turned away (429): total (all of the groups) and by group: per-address rate limit refusals by address group (platform_ranges: addresses in the AI platforms' published ranges, which have a higher limit; everyone_else: every other caller), then, regardless of address, server_busy (0.10.0 only: shared database queue pressure; 0 from 0.10.1, which removed that refusal) and too_many_clients (the server was tracking as many addresses as it can); null on days before it was counted. restarts (from 0.10.0; null before): how many times the server started that day; callers and parts_asked distinct count a caller or part seen on both sides of a restart twice. lcsc_lookups (from 0.10.2; null before): how jlc_get_part's LCSC-code lookups and jlc_stock_check's one-code queries were answered, one each: snapshot (the daily snapshot, no request), live (answered from a live lookup, including its 1-hour cache), fallback (JLCPCB didn't answer and the snapshot did: live_failed in the reply) and live_failed (the live lookup failed and nothing answered instead: the error). distributor_apps (from 0.10.2; null before): calls to mouser_get_part, digikey_get_part and part_lifecycle by app, and how many were rate_limited; a call counts under the app its address last connected with (remembered for 10 minutes after the address's last connection or tool call), else under unknown. distributor_limits (from 0.10.3; null before): for mouser and digikey, held_back counts lookups not sent, by cause: minute_cap and daily_count (this server's limits), address_daily (the address's daily cap), distributor_daily, distributor_minute and distributor_refused (pauses after the distributor refused), other; it adds up to distributors rate_limited. held_back_hours: the same by UTC hour. refusals: sent requests the distributor refused (daily, minute, refused). datasheet_links (from 0.10.3; null before): visits to datasheet_pdf links: reused (no JLCPCB request), signed (one was made), waited (of those, after waiting for a slot), refused (429), failed (502), not_found (404). db_waits (from 0.10.3; null before): database jobs (jobs), those that waited at least 0.1 s for a worker (waited), the longest wait (longest_ms), and waited_hours and longest_ms_hours by UTC hour; components: the same for the component catalog alone. In totals the longest is the maximum. lifecycle_inputs (from 0.10.4; null before): part_lifecycle entries by input form, before catalog resolution: bare_number, with_manufacturer or lcsc_code; invalid inputs aren't counted. Counts only, no part numbers or maker names. bad_request_reasons (from 0.10.5; null before): one fixed label per bad_request, separate from reasons; arg:<declared parameter or unknown_argument>:<fixed error type> for argument validation, all_inputs_invalid for invalid batches, unknown_tool for unknown tools. tool_apps (from 0.10.5; null before): each tool's calls and every outcome by app, up to 50 named apps per tool today, later new names count as other; past UTC days keep the 14 busiest apps by calls plus other, which sums every outcome from the rest (compacted on rollover, load, save and summary); same app attribution as distributor_apps. latency (from 0.10.5; null before): each tool's bucket counts and p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, counting ok, similar_only, not_found and failed only; latency_bounds_ms gives inclusive upper bounds, with one final open bucket; percentiles are bucket upper bounds (null for an empty histogram or the open bucket). tool_apps, latency and popular_terms are kept for the last 30 days only, cleared from older days on rollover, load, save and summary, even with no new calls. popular_terms (from 0.10.5; null before): top 200 query tokens by occurrences, each counted once per call, up to 20 tokens per query, for jlc_search, jlc_stock_check, cse_search, board_search and sensor_recommend except bad_request. Only tokens from at least 10 distinct callers that UTC day are retained; all platform addresses count as one caller, other IPv6 addresses by /48. This is a popularity heuristic, not an anonymity guarantee against someone controlling many addresses. Below-threshold tokens and salted caller hashes stay in memory only (20,000 tokens, 10 hashes each). No phrases. A restart keeps retained counts but resets the threshold for new tokens; totals sums retained daily counts, keeping the top 200. versions (from 0.10.5; null before): server starts by running version. upstream_status (from 0.10.5; null before): one class per sent request per source: 2xx, 3xx, 4xx, 429 (separate from 4xx), 5xx, timeout, connection, challenge, too_large, cancelled or other_error. Cutovers from 0.10.5: mouser_get_part misses count part_not_found instead of no_results; jlc_stock_check's no_results splits into no_results_filtered, no_results_part_number and no_results_words; jlc_search's part_number_not_in_stock becomes part_number_sold_out or part_number_unknown, using a label-only lookup of previously listed parts. Historical labels and counts are kept. Failed calls also produce one labels-only WARNING per UTC minute.
